newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals edge up, end losing streak.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals edge up, end losing streak.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based gold and platinum futures ended firmer on Thursday for the first time in five sessions, supported by indications that bullion prices were finding support, although the futures received little direction from the foreign exchange market, traders said.
TOCOM benchmark October 1997 gold settled four higher at 1,342 yen per gram, after hitting a seven-week low of 1,338 on Wednesday. The other months went out two to six better.
Gold bullion ended at $378.15/45 an ounce, little changed from New York's closing quote of $378.20/80 and Tokyo's Wednesday close of $378.20/50.
Bullion prices have moved steadily lower since last week's probe of the upside failed to breach resistance at $385, with dealers now focusing on key support at $377.

One Australian dealer noted good two-way business despite the narrow range during Asia's trading hours. He said gold traders there were eyeing the Australian dollar's surge in the past two days, which prompted a slump in prices that Australian producers could receive for their output.
A Japanese broker said speculative short-covering helped lift TOCOM gold today, although private investors' sizable long positions in the December contract still hang over the market.

Japanese traders also said Tokyo's bullion prices this week returned to their usual premium over benchmark loco London, after trading flat or at a discount to London for more than two months. They said demand from Japan's jewellery sector, while still sluggish, had picked up slightly.

In the other precious metals, TOCOM October platinum ended six higher at 1,373 yen per gram, October palladium was up one at 428 yen per gram, and October silver was 0.6 firmer at 178.6 yen per 10 grams.
